Neha / Dev — thanks for the heads-up. I reviewed EdgeCorp's subcontractor list and Neha's draft redline. A few legal points for the reply we should send to EdgeCorp: 

1) Prior written consent / permitted replacements
- We should accept a clause that allows Redwood to engage subcontractors for infrastructure and managed services, but require prior written notice and the right to object for any subcontractor that will receive unredacted customer content or PII. Proposed short text: "Customer consent shall not be unreasonably withheld for subcontractors used solely for infrastructure services; where a subcontractor may access Customer Content, Redwood will obtain prior written approval, which shall not be unreasonably withheld."

2) DPA flow-down requirement
- We must flow down the DPA obligations (data use, retention, deletion) to NimbusLogix. Add explicit requirement that subcontractors sign an equivalent DPA or be bound directly by the EdgeCorp DPA terms.

3) Audit & certifications
- Request SOC2 Type II (or ISO27001) within 30 days of onboarding and annual attestations. For newly added subprocessors, allow a 30-day window to provide evidence.

4) Access controls & encryption
- Require TLS in transit, SSE for logs at rest, and key management responsibilities clarified. If Nimbus will only receive redacted/aggregated logs, note that in order form annex.

5) Limited liability and indemnity
- We should cap exposure to the Order Form's liability caps and avoid open-ended indemnities tied to subprocessor actions.

Operational question for Dev: can we guarantee that NimbusLogix will only ever see redacted logs (no persistent KV cache access)? If not, we should mark the subcontractor as needing elevated review and consider dedicated capacity.

If Dev confirms redaction is feasible, I'll draft an email to EdgeCorp with the proposed language and the redline attached.

—Lauren

Laura / Neha — quick technical note:

- Runtime behavior: NimbusLogix will receive forwarded log streams from our observability pipeline. These are not pulled from KV cache or model context. By default logs include request metadata and anonymized traces; payloads containing user content are redacted by our logging filters.
- Tenant isolation: we can route EdgeCorp logs to a dedicated ingestion workspace and apply an additional redaction layer before forwarding. That would prevent any KV cache or model access.
- Capacity/Cost: enabling a dedicated ingestion workspace for EdgeCorp + on-demand parsing workers will add an estimated $1,200/month and a 5–10% increase in ingestion latency during peak.
- Evidence: NimbusLogix has not been onboarded before; we require their SOC2 attestation. If EdgeCorp can accept a 30-day window for evidence, we can proceed with conditional onboarding.

Internal ref: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-5729 (ops changes for dedicated ingestion routing)

If legal wants strict redaction-only confirmation, we can implement a signed runbook that shows the pipeline and redaction steps (takes ~3 business days to produce).

—Dev
